children: Commodity markets traded mixed on September 2, with oil prices rising nearly 1% in early trade, while gold held its decline amid Middle East attacks.

Oil prices rose nearly 1% in early trade on Wednesday, extending the previous session's surge, as concerns over supply disruption intensified after the U.S. and Iran exchanged strikes overnight, dimming hopes for a quick easing of tensions in the Middle East.
Brent crude futures rose 87 cents, or 0.92%, to $95.52 a barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude futures climbed 80 cents, or 0.89%, to $91.02.
Both contracts soared more than $4 on Tuesday, marking Brent's largest gain since July 24 and WTI's largest since July 23.
Gold held a decline as attacks in the Middle East and a global bond selloff ratcheted up bets the Federal Reserve may need to raise interest rates to rein in inflation.
Bullion was trading around $4,330 an ounce, after falling almost 6% over the previous three sessions to a two-week low.
Among other precious metals, silver was stable at $64.11 an ounce. Platinum and palladium edged lower.
The dollar held firm on Wednesday as renewed hostilities in the Middle East pushed oil prices higher and revived inflation concerns.
The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, was at 99.74.

title: Commodity Corner: Oil rises on supply disruption concerns; gold extends decline
